summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Credit Union Chartering & Associational Common Bond Rules
summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration Board issued a final rule amending 12 CFR Part 701’s Chartering and Field of Membership Manual to clarify how associational common bonds are determined for single associational and multiple common bond federal credit unions. Effective January 4, 2027, the rule provides that requiring members to buy a good, product, or service from a group as a condition of membership no longer automatically disqualifies that group from recognition as an association. NCUA will instead assess the totality of the circumstances—using detailed criteria and examples distinguishing a primarily client-customer relationship, which still does not qualify, from an incidental one—and will simplify review of pre-approved groups. The rule finalizes the April 8, 2026 proposal after 18 comments, nearly all supportive, while rejecting a bankers association’s objection that the change would erode statutory field-of-membership limits. The amendments do not apply to occupational common bond charters, community charters, or federally insured state-chartered credit unions, and NCUA expects them to reduce confusion and improve access to credit union services while preserving limits against unqualified client-customer groups.

summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Reserve Regulation D & Depository Institution Reserve Requirements
summary_responses.response: The Federal Reserve issued a final rule amending Regulation D to reflect the required annual indexing of the reserve requirement exemption amount and low reserve tranche for 2027. Because total reservable liabilities fell 2.4% from $21.103 trillion to $20.588 trillion between June 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, the exemption amount remains $39.2 million, unchanged from 2026. Net transaction accounts rose 2.7% from $17.012 trillion to $17.465 trillion over the same period, so the low reserve tranche increases to $688.5 million from $674.1 million, effective for institutions beginning January 1, 2027. The rule is effective December 18, 2026, but the statutory indexing will not change depository institutions' reserve requirements, which have remained zero since March 2020. The Board adopted the amendments without notice-and-comment rulemaking, finding good cause because they are ministerial statutory adjustments, and determined the Regulatory Flexibility Act and Paperwork Reduction Act requirements do not apply or involve no collections of information.

summary_responses.subtopic: Postal Regulatory Commission Competitive Product Rate & Filing Proceedings
summary_responses.response: The Postal Regulatory Commission opened Docket No. CP2027-1 after the Postal Service filed a November 12, 2026 notice of planned rate and classification changes for Competitive products, scheduled to take effect January 17, 2027. The filing, supported by Governors’ Decision No. 26-8, includes broad average increases of about 5.9 percent for Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Parcel Select and USPS Ground Advantage, 16 percent for nonstandard fees, and roughly 7.9 percent for many international products. Major classification changes include a permanent flat 11 percent fuel surcharge on those domestic package products, later intended to adjust weekly based on Energy Information Administration fuel prices, plus a 20 percent repricing fee for postage underpayments or overpayments caused by inaccurate dimensions or weight. The plan also renames the Noncompliance Fee as the Dimension and Weight Noncompliance Fee, expands Premium Forwarding Service options, adds a Shipping Label Noncompliance Fee, increases international flat-rate envelope and box price groups from 8 to 20, adds USPS Delivered Duty Paid as an International Priority Airmail option, and revises international country group assignments. The Commission invites public comments by December 4, 2026 on whether the changes comply with applicable statutes and regulations, and it appointed Christopher Mohr as Public Representative.

summary_responses.response: The SEC published notice that Texas Stock Exchange LLC filed a proposed rule change on November 10, 2026, with changes proposed to take effect November 2, 2026, and is soliciting public comments. TXSE says the changes are intended for business and competitive reasons to incentivize displayed liquidity and are consistent with the Securities Exchange Act, while the SEC is seeking comments rather than announcing final approval.

summary_responses.subtopic: Aerospace Rotorcraft Structural Engineering & FAA Airworthiness Directives
summary_responses.response: The FAA has proposed a new airworthiness directive for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH EC135 and EC635T2+ helicopters, all serial numbers up to and including 1276, after determining that the manufacturer’s service material lacks complete instructions for inspections following a hard landing. The unsafe condition could cause tail rotor control damage to go undetected, potentially leading to component or system failure and reduced helicopter control. The proposal would require a one-time inspection of the tail rotor control system within 12 months of the AD’s effective date, corrective actions if discrepancies are found, and revision of the aircraft maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness and the approved maintenance or inspection program. It incorporates EASA AD 2020-0102 by reference with FAA-specific differences, including excluding certain EC635 variants without FAA type certificates and requiring corrective actions approved by the FAA, EASA, or the AHD Design Organization Approval. Comments are due January 4, 2027; the FAA estimates the rule would affect 289 US-registered helicopters, with inspection and maintenance-program revision costs of about $340 and $85 per helicopter, respectively.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: The National Park Service issued a final rule amending Mammoth Cave National Park’s special regulations to allow bicycles on about 37 miles of multi-use trails and horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, effective December 21, 2026. The rule authorizes the superintendent to designate 12 trails for bicycle use, removing the Maple Springs Connector and White Oak Trails while retaining the Mammoth Cave Railroad Bike & Hike Trail, splitting Big Hollow into three segments, and adding eight planned new trails. It implements part of the park’s Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment and the December 2024 Finding of No Significant Impact, which selected an alternative adding about 66 miles of land-based trails to improve access and sustainability. The EA evaluated trail surfaces, soil conditions, maintenance costs, safety, user conflicts, and resource protection, and new construction will use sustainable techniques and mitigation to limit erosion and vegetation impacts. The superintendent must notify the public of designated trails through standard NPS methods, may allow e-bikes on trails open to traditional bicycles, and the horse provision relaxes the general ban on equestrian use of park roads for that specific road.
